clue.text: Benjamin is willing to give a blessing

parts.note: Ben is the short form of the name Benjamin
on means willing or game, as in 'I'm on for that'

explanation.surface: A man named Benjamin is happy to bestow his blessing on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A benison is an old literary word for a blessing or benediction.

clue.text: Pants a lot

definitions.meaning: ... is a British word for loose trousers, as in Oxford ...
... of means plenty of, as in ... of time

explanation.definitionFit: Bags are baggy trousers, and 'bags of' is informal for a large amount.

clue.text: A river once more going over the falls

indicators.note: in a down clue, going over turns the run of pieces so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: once more means again

explanation.surface: Someone takes a river trip again and is swept over a waterfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going over' turns ARAGAIN (A, R for river, AGAIN) end to end.
explanation.definitionFit: Niagara is the famous set of waterfalls on the US-Canada border.

clue.text: Animal, one of a deadly collection

definitions.meaning: a slow-moving tree-dwelling mammal of South America
one of the seven deadly sins, laziness

explanation.definitionFit: Sloth is both a tree-hanging mammal and idleness, one of the seven deadly sins.

clue.text: Patching damaged attire

indicators.note: damaged signals that the letters of the word before are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is mending clothes that have been torn.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightcap is a cap worn in bed, an item of attire for sleeping.

clue.text: Headgear, green, originally designed in part of Massachusetts

parts.note: a cap is a piece of headgear
eco- is a prefix meaning green or environmentally friendly

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A hat in an environmentally friendly style was first created in New England.
explanation.walkthrough: CAPE COD is the hook-shaped peninsula of Massachusetts.
explanation.definitionFit: Cape Cod is a well-known peninsula forming part of the state of Massachusetts.

clue.text: Boxer, possibly American, in English rings

indicators.note: rings means encircles, so the clue words surround the letters wanted

explanation.surface: A boxer, perhaps from the United States, fights in rings in England.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a pugilist and boxing rings; in fact 'rings' says the words American, in English enclose the answer, and the boxer is a dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxer is a breed of dog, so it is an example of a dog-like animal.

clue.text: Thrust into a difficult situation, tar has to attack on board

parts.note: pitch is a black tarry substance
in chess a fork is an attack on two pieces at once

explanation.surface: A sailor is pushed into a crisis and has to launch an assault aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tar' looks like a sailor and 'on board' like a ship, but it is pitch, and the board is a chessboard.
explanation.definitionFit: To pitchfork someone is to thrust them suddenly into a situation, an idiomatic sense.

clue.text: Body or bodywork?

parts.note: a dead body, or the shell of a vehicle read as a motor's casing

explanation.definitionFit: A carcase is a dead body, and read in two parts it suggests the body of a motor vehicle.

clue.text: Irish shopping centre with very little prestige

parts.note: Down is a county of Northern Ireland
a market is a place for shopping

explanation.surface: An Irish mall is not considered a classy place.
explanation.definitionFit: Downmarket means cheap and of low status, the opposite of upmarket.

clue.text: Fascinating periodical put together in South Wales

parts.note: glam, short for glamorous, means alluring or fascinating
an organ is a newspaper or magazine, a periodical

explanation.surface: An alluring magazine is produced in South Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: Glamorgan is an old county of South Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Glamorgan is a historic county located in South Wales, so it is a place there.

clue.text: Disconcerted, finished talking

indicators.note: talking signals that the word must be spoken to give the entry

parts.note: through means finished, as in 'I'm through with it'

explanation.surface: Someone flustered stops speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw someone is to disconcert them, so threw is the past tense equivalent.

clue.text: Flu jab renewed confidence

definitions.meaning: a boost or fillip that restores morale

explanation.definitionFit: Literally an injection in the upper limb, and figuratively an idiom for a boost of encouragement.

clue.text: Having got the wind up, is initially trapped in the current of air

indicators.note: in tells us the preceding letters sit inside the next word

parts.note: a draught is a current of air

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Someone panics on being caught in a gust of wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got the wind up' is British slang for being frightened, not about breeze.
explanation.definitionFit: Distraught means extremely upset or agitated, matching the idiom for being scared.

clue.text: Probably, one day, god will be in the centre of it

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.text: will be in the centre of
indicators.note: these words place the god inside the middle of the phrase one day

parts.note: taken as written
Ares is the Greek god of war

explanation.surface: Probably some deity will one day find itself at the heart of things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' refers back to 'one day', the phrase whose middle receives the god.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'I dare say' means I suppose, that is, probably.

clue.text: I left Catherine for a short time, in preparation for jump

indicators.note: in preparation suggests the letters being got ready, rearranged into shape
left means taken away, so the letter is removed

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned Catherine briefly to get ready for a leap.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing I from Catherine leaves CATHERNE; add T and rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrechat is a ballet jump in which the dancer crosses the feet in the air.

clue.text: Not likely to be seen in dreadnought

parts.note: read as dread plus nought, the parts swapped give nought (none) and dread (terror)

explanation.surface: Fearlessness is unlikely to be found aboard a battleship.
explanation.walkthrough: A dreadnought is a type of battleship; split it as dread and nought.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation 'no fear' is British slang for certainly not, not likely.

clue.text: Make an effort to visit London

definitions.meaning: to do something lavishly and with enthusiasm
town in British usage often means London

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to do something with great enthusiasm, and literally to travel up to the capital.

clue.text: Worry disrupting attempt to reach agreement

indicators.note: disrupting means breaking into, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a try is an attempt
eat means worry, as in 'what's eating you?'

explanation.surface: Anxiety gets in the way of efforts to reach a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A treaty is a formal agreement between states.

clue.text: Proteas flourished in the grass

indicators.note: flourished, as in waved about, signals the letters being moved around

explanation.surface: South African flowers thrived in the lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Esparto is a tough grass of Spain and North Africa used for paper and rope.

clue.text: Confident mates can be found by river

parts.note: cock is British slang for a mate, as in 'wotcha, cock'
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Self-assured friends are spotted beside a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocksure means overconfident or arrogantly certain.

clue.text: Country with sovereignty, so to speak

definitions.text: Country with sovereignty, so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak signals that the words are to be said out loud

parts.note: the country is the UK and sovereignty is reign

explanation.surface: An independent nation is described in a roundabout manner.
explanation.walkthrough: UK plus REIGN said out loud gives the entry, and the whole clue describes it too.
explanation.definitionFit: Ukraine is a sovereign nation in eastern Europe, an independent country.

clue.text: Note, over half of dairymen appear to be in flight

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: half of takes the first four of the word's eight letters

explanation.surface: Some milkmen appear to be flying.
explanation.definitionFit: Midair describes something up in the sky, airborne or in flight.

clue.text: Everything's hunky-dory in this selection from the dessert menu

definitions.text: Everything's hunky-dory in this selection from the dessert menu

parts.words: Everything's hunky-dory in this selection from the dessert menu
parts.note: a phrase for perfect neatness, read as asking for a pudding from the sweets list

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means perfectly neat and tidy, and literally could be choosing a fruit pastry dessert.

clue.text: Doctor wanting to possess swamp

parts.note: to own is to possess

explanation.surface: A physician wants to acquire marshland.
explanation.definitionFit: To swamp something is to flood or overwhelm it with water.

clue.text: Openers in Surrey team usually nerveless, making hit for six

indicators.note: openers are the first letters, taken from each of the following words

explanation.surface: Surrey's opening batsmen, usually calm, smash a big hit at cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: To hit for six is British slang, from cricket, for shocking or devastating someone; Surrey is a county cricket side.
explanation.definitionFit: To be hit for six figuratively is to be stunned, so stun is the same shock.

clue.text: Waist measurement, right? Wrong!

indicators.note: wrong signals that the letters of the word are put in a wrong order

explanation.surface: Someone checks a waist size and finds it incorrect.
explanation.definitionFit: Girth is the measurement around the middle, as in a waist size.

clue.text: Champion has a game point

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback
the gist is the main point

explanation.surface: A winner holds a sporting match point.
explanation.definitionFit: An apologist champions or defends a cause, so the noun means a supporter.

clue.text: Foot of pig or horse

definitions.meaning: a pig's foot cooked as food
a horse bred for harness racing at a trot

explanation.definitionFit: A pig's trotter is its foot, and a trotter is also a harness-racing horse.

clue.text: Stuff making grandmother enthusiastic

parts.note: nan is an informal name for a grandmother
keen means enthusiastic

explanation.surface: Something makes Granny eager.
explanation.definitionFit: Nankeen is a yellowish cotton fabric, and stuff is an old word for cloth.
